text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128]},"shared_memory_limit":49152,"weights":{"traffic":1.0,"launches":0.5,"pipeline":2.0,"footprint":1.0},"rationale":"Workload is 4096x4096x1024 float16 GEMM with float32 accumulation; every allowed block_M/block_N in {64,128} and block_K in {32,64} divides M=N=4096 and K=1024, so the full domain remains feasible and threads stays fixed at 128. Shared-memory estimate 2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages peaks above 49152 (e.g. 128x128x64x3 = 98304), so the 49152-byte limit meaningfully prunes high-stage large-tile tuples while admitting configurations such as 128x128x32x3 and 128x64x64x2. Feedback shows the solver selected a single-stage large-tile tuple, indicating footprint and traffic terms were dominating pipeline depth; I therefore raise the pipeline weight from 0.5 to 2.0 to push selection toward deeper K-blocking/pipelining that can reduce exposed operand latency, while keeping traffic and footprint at 1.0 to still favor large tiles and bounded shared-memory pressure, and retaining a mild 0.5 launches weight since 4096-wide outputs already yield few launches. These remain analytic objective weights only; compilation is still blocked (no sm_121a adapter, tilelang/nvcc/nvdisasm unavailable), no simulation timings exist, and CPU-shadow correctness plus latency do not establish CUDA correctness or GB10 performance. No SASS was inspected, no GPU results are claimed, and actual resource validity and performance on GB10 remain unverified."}
